options: молчание
молчания
молчанию
молчанием
cases.explain: "Молчание" is the subject of the verb "наступило" (fell/set in), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Необходимо отправиться по делу, и таким образом не помешаю, — прибавил он и стал вставать со ___.
options: стул
стула
стулу
стулом
cases.translation: "I must attend to some business, and so I won't be in the way," he added, and began to rise from his chair.
cases.explain: The preposition "со" (a form of "с", meaning "from/off") governs the genitive case here, giving "стула."

cases.sentence: Я же, при всем желании, никак не мог вчера поспешить к ___.
options: встреча
встречи
встрече
встречу
cases.translation: For my part, however much I wished, I simply could not hurry to the meeting yesterday.
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (to/toward) governs the dative case, giving "встрече."

cases.sentence: Он встал со стула и взял ___.
options: шляпа
шляпы
шляпе
шляпу
cases.translation: He rose from his chair and took his hat.
cases.explain: "Шляпу" is the direct object of the transitive verb "взял" (took), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Петр Петрович, — с ___ произнесла Пульхерия Александровна, — доказательство тому, что мы с Дуней не приняли ваших слов в дурную сторону.
options: достоинство
достоинства
достоинству
достоинством
cases.translation: "Pyotr Petrovich," said Pulkheria Alexandrovna with dignity, "proof of this is that Dunya and I did not take your words badly."
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) governs the instrumental case, giving "достоинством" (with dignity).

cases.sentence: Вы всё Родиона вините, а вы и сами об нем давеча неправду написали в ___.
options: письмо
письма
письму
письме
cases.translation: You keep blaming Rodion, but you yourself wrote an untruth about him earlier in the letter.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" (in), indicating location, governs the prepositional case, giving "письме."

cases.sentence: Необходимо отправиться по ___, и таким образом не помешаю.
options: дело
дела
делу
делом
cases.translation: I must attend to some business, and so I won't be in the way.
cases.explain: The preposition "по" (about/regarding) governs the dative case, giving "делу."

cases.sentence: Ах, нет, Петр Петрович, мы были очень обескуражены, — с особой ___ поспешила заявить Пульхерия Александровна.
options: интонация
интонации
интонацию
интонацией
cases.translation: "Oh no, Pyotr Petrovich, we were very discouraged," Pulkheria Alexandrovna hastened to declare with a particular tone.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) governs the instrumental case, giving "интонацией."

reading.ru: Было уж почти восемь часов; оба спешили к Бакалееву, чтобы прийти раньше Лужина.
reading.question: Why are Raskolnikov and Razumikhin hurrying as the chapter begins?
options: To arrive at Bakaleyev's before Luzhin
To catch a train
To meet Porfiry again
To avoid Svidrigailov
reading.correct: To arrive at Bakaleyev's before Luzhin
reading.explain: It was nearly eight o'clock, and both were hurrying to Bakaleyev's lodgings to arrive before Luzhin.

reading.ru: Это был Свидригайлов, тот самый помещик, в доме которого была обижена сестра, когда служила у них гувернанткой.
reading.question: Who does Raskolnikov explain the mysterious visitor was, and how does he connect to Dunya?
options: Svidrigailov, the landowner in whose house Dunya was insulted while working as governess
Luzhin, Dunya's fiance
Porfiry, investigating the murder
A former classmate of Raskolnikov
reading.correct: Svidrigailov, the landowner in whose house Dunya was insulted while working as governess
reading.explain: Raskolnikov identifies the visitor as Svidrigailov, the landowner whose household Dunya served in as governess and was mistreated.

reading.ru: — Ты его видел? — спросил Раскольников после некоторого молчания.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov ask Razumikhin after a pause in their conversation?
options: Whether he had seen Svidrigailov
Whether he had seen Porfiry
Whether he had seen Dunya
Whether he had seen the murder weapon
reading.correct: Whether he had seen Svidrigailov
reading.explain: After a silence, Raskolnikov asks Razumikhin directly whether he had seen him (Svidrigailov).

reading.ru: я памятлив на лица.
reading.question: What does Razumikhin claim about his memory for faces?
options: That he has a good memory for faces and would recognize the man among a thousand
That he never remembers faces
That he forgets people quickly
That he only remembers voices, not faces
reading.correct: That he has a good memory for faces and would recognize the man among a thousand
reading.explain: Razumikhin insists he remembers clearly and is good at remembering faces, claiming he'd recognize the man out of a thousand.

reading.ru: может быть, я в самом деле помешанный и только призрак видел!
reading.question: What troubling doubt does Raskolnikov express about his own sanity?
options: That perhaps he really is insane and only saw a phantom
That he is certain Svidrigailov is real
That he never doubts his own mind
That Razumikhin is the one who is mad
reading.correct: That perhaps he really is insane and only saw a phantom
reading.explain: Raskolnikov wonders aloud whether he really is deranged and only saw a ghost/phantom rather than a real person.

reading.ru: Эх, Родя! Расстроили тебя опять!..
reading.question: How does Razumikhin react to Raskolnikov's doubts about his own sanity?
options: He expresses concern that Raskolnikov has been upset again
He laughs it off as a joke
He agrees that Raskolnikov is losing his mind
He ignores the comment entirely
reading.correct: He expresses concern that Raskolnikov has been upset again
reading.explain: Razumikhin exclaims with concern that Raskolnikov has been upset/distressed once more.

reading.ru: В коридоре они столкнулись с Лужиным: он явился ровно в восемь часов
reading.question: When do Raskolnikov and Razumikhin encounter Luzhin?
options: In the corridor, as Luzhin arrives exactly at eight o'clock
At the train station
At Porfiry's office
In Svidrigailov's apartment
reading.correct: In the corridor, as Luzhin arrives exactly at eight o'clock
reading.explain: They run into Luzhin in the corridor; he had arrived exactly at eight o'clock and was looking for the right room.

reading.ru: Надеюсь, путешествие прошло благополучно?
reading.question: What polite question does Luzhin ask Pulkheria Alexandrovna upon arrival?
options: Whether their journey went well
Whether she received his letter
Whether Dunya is feeling better
Whether Raskolnikov is home
reading.correct: Whether their journey went well
reading.explain: Luzhin formally asks Pulkheria Alexandrovna whether their journey passed safely and well.

reading.ru: Велика так называемая «матушка Россия»…
reading.question: What remark does Luzhin make about Russia's national roads?
options: That Russia's roads are very long and vast, "Mother Russia" is great
That the roads are being repaired
That the roads are dangerous at night
That the roads are better than in Europe
reading.correct: That Russia's roads are very long and vast, "Mother Russia" is great
reading.explain: Luzhin comments on the length of Russia's national roads, remarking on how great so-called "Mother Russia" is.

reading.ru: Марфа Петровна умерла, вы слышали?
reading.question: What news does Pulkheria Alexandrovna bring up to fill the awkward silence?
options: That Marfa Petrovna has died
That Dunya is engaged again
That Raskolnikov is ill
That Luzhin has lost his job
reading.correct: That Marfa Petrovna has died
reading.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna, resorting to her go-to topic, brings up the news that Marfa Petrovna has died.

reading.ru: Господи! Да неужели он и тут не оставит Дунечку в покое?
reading.question: What fear does Pulkheria Alexandrovna express upon learning Svidrigailov has come to Petersburg?
options: That he will not leave Dunechka alone even here
That he will harm Luzhin
That he will demand money from them
That he will report Raskolnikov to the police
reading.correct: That he will not leave Dunechka alone even here
reading.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna cries out in fear that Svidrigailov will not leave Dunechka in peace even in Petersburg.

reading.ru: он способствовал ускоренному ходу вещей, так сказать, нравственным влиянием обиды
reading.question: What does Luzhin suggest about Svidrigailov's role in Marfa Petrovna's death?
options: That he may have hastened it through the moral influence of an insult
That he directly poisoned her
That he had nothing at all to do with it
That he saved her life at the last moment
reading.correct: That he may have hastened it through the moral influence of an insult
reading.explain: Luzhin suggests Svidrigailov may have contributed to hastening events through the moral effect of an insult/offense.

reading.ru: Я слышала, напротив, что этот Филипп сам удавился.
reading.question: What does Dunya say she heard about how Filipp died, contradicting Luzhin's account?
options: That Filipp hanged himself
That Filipp drowned accidentally
That Filipp died of old age
That Filipp was murdered by Svidrigailov directly
reading.correct: That Filipp hanged himself
reading.explain: Dunya states that, contrary to what is implied, she heard that Filipp hanged himself.

reading.ru: Он сейчас приходил ко мне, — сказал вдруг Раскольников, в первый раз прерывая молчание.
reading.question: What surprising announcement does Raskolnikov make, breaking his silence?
options: That Svidrigailov had just come to see him
That he is engaged to be married
That he has decided to leave Petersburg
That he has resolved his conflict with Porfiry
reading.correct: That Svidrigailov had just come to see him
reading.explain: Raskolnikov breaks his silence for the first time to announce that Svidrigailov had just visited him.

reading.ru: — Это действительная правда, — сорвалось у Лужина.
reading.question: What does Luzhin blurt out when Raskolnikov mentions the three thousand rubles left to Dunya?
options: That it is indeed the actual truth
That it is a complete lie
That he already knew about it
That the sum is too small to matter
reading.correct: That it is indeed the actual truth
reading.explain: Luzhin blurts out that this (the inheritance) is indeed the actual truth, confirming Raskolnikov's statement.

reading.ru: Раскольников замолчал и обратился к своему чаю.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do when pressed further about Svidrigailov's proposal to Dunya?
options: He falls silent and turns to his tea instead of answering
He explains everything in detail immediately
He storms out of the room
He accuses Luzhin of eavesdropping
reading.correct: He falls silent and turns to his tea instead of answering
reading.explain: Raskolnikov says he'll tell them later, then falls silent and turns his attention to his tea.

reading.ru: не исполнена единственно по моему настоянию
reading.question: According to Dunya, why was Luzhin's request to exclude Raskolnikov from the meeting not honored?
options: Solely because Dunya herself insisted on it
Because Raskolnikov refused to leave
Because Pulkheria Alexandrovna forgot the request
Because Razumikhin objected
reading.correct: Solely because Dunya herself insisted on it
reading.explain: Dunya explains that Luzhin's request was not fulfilled solely because she herself had insisted otherwise.

reading.ru: Ценя и, так сказать, обожая вас, я в то же время весьма и весьма могу не любить кого-нибудь из ваших домашних.
reading.question: What contradictory claim does Luzhin make about his feelings for Dunya versus her family?
options: That he can value and adore her while still disliking members of her household
That he loves her family more than her
That he has never disliked anyone in her family
That his feelings for her are purely practical
reading.correct: That he can value and adore her while still disliking members of her household
reading.explain: Luzhin argues that while valuing and adoring Dunya, he can still very much dislike some of her household members, meaning Raskolnikov.

reading.ru: Раскольников молча и язвительно улыбнулся, Разумихина всего передернуло
reading.question: How do Raskolnikov and Razumikhin react as Luzhin grows increasingly self-righteous?
options: Raskolnikov smiles caustically in silence, while Razumikhin flinches all over
Both laugh out loud together
Both leave the room in disgust
Raskolnikov argues loudly while Razumikhin stays calm
reading.correct: Raskolnikov smiles caustically in silence, while Razumikhin flinches all over
reading.explain: The text describes Raskolnikov smiling silently and sarcastically, while Razumikhin winces/flinches entirely.

reading.ru: вы и сами об нем давеча неправду написали в письме
reading.question: What accusation does Pulkheria Alexandrovna make against Luzhin regarding his letter about Raskolnikov?
options: That he himself wrote an untruth about Raskolnikov in his letter
That he never sent any letter at all
That the letter was addressed to the wrong person
That the letter praised Raskolnikov excessively
reading.correct: That he himself wrote an untruth about Raskolnikov in his letter
reading.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna, growing bolder, points out that Luzhin himself wrote something untrue about Raskolnikov earlier in his letter.

reading.ru: Я посадил ее сегодня рядом с маменькой и с Дуней.
reading.question: What defiant action does Raskolnikov reveal he took regarding the unfortunate girl Luzhin maligned?
options: He seated her today next to his mother and Dunya
He gave her all his remaining money
He sent her away from the city
He asked Luzhin to apologize to her
reading.correct: He seated her today next to his mother and Dunya
reading.explain: Raskolnikov reveals that he has already introduced the girl into society by seating her next to his mother and Dunya that very day.

reading.ru: вы рассчитывали на нашу беспомощность
reading.question: What does Dunya accuse Luzhin of, based on his remark about the inheritance news?
options: That he had been counting on their helplessness
That he had planned to marry someone else
That he had lied about his income
That he had never intended to marry her
reading.correct: That he had been counting on their helplessness
reading.explain: Dunya remarks irritably that Luzhin's comment suggests he had been counting on their helplessness.

reading.ru: я уж не ворочусь никогда.
reading.question: What ultimatum does Luzhin give Dunya if he walks out the door now?
options: That he will never come back
That he will return within the hour
That he will report her to the authorities
That he will demand his letters back
reading.correct: That he will never come back
reading.explain: Luzhin warns Dunya that if he leaves through that door now with such a send-off, he will never return.

reading.ru: это вы нас по рукам и по ногам связали, а не мы вас!
reading.question: How does Pulkheria Alexandrovna respond to Luzhin's complaint about being tied down by his word and expenses?
options: She retorts that he has bound them hand and foot, not the other way around
She apologizes for the inconvenience
She agrees to pay him back immediately
She begs him to reconsider
reading.correct: She retorts that he has bound them hand and foot, not the other way around
reading.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna angrily retorts that it is Luzhin who has bound them hand and foot, not the reverse.

reading.ru: редко кто-нибудь уносил на кого в своем сердце столько злобной ненависти
reading.question: How intense is Luzhin's hatred of Raskolnikov as he leaves the apartment for good?
options: Rarely has anyone carried away such intense, malicious hatred for another person
He feels only mild irritation
He feels sympathy for Raskolnikov despite everything
He quickly forgets the whole incident
reading.correct: Rarely has anyone carried away such intense, malicious hatred for another person
reading.explain: The narrator remarks that rarely does anyone carry away in his heart as much spiteful hatred as Luzhin now bears toward Raskolnikov.
